metadata.case_name: AQSA RANA v. TSUI LUK PUI

injuries.description: A 3 x 3 cm skin defect was found over right foot dorsum. She received two operations as excisional debridement of wound on 25 October 2004 and debridement and split-thickness skin graft on 31 October 2004.
source: A 3 x 3 cm skin defect was found over right foot dorsum. Her ankle and toe movement were intact sensation and circulation of her right foot and ankle were normal. There was no other injury. She received two operations as excisional debridement of wound on 25 October 2004 and debridement and split-thickness skin graft on 31 October 2004. She was discharged on 13 November 2004. She was last seen on 17 November 2004. At that time both donor site of skin graft and her right foot wound healed. She will be follow up in our out-patient clinic later.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified open wound of ankle or foot

injuries.description: Donor site scar in the right thigh (8 cm x 7 cm) with mild hypersensitivity at the skin graft donor site.
source: Aqsa is now left with an unsightly scar on the right ankle and foot, mild hypersensitivity at the skin graft donor site in the right thigh and pain in the bone under the grafted site on rough contact.
This scar from the donor site is 8 cm x 7 cm and the scar on the right ankle and foot is 16 cm x 5 cm.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified injuries to the hip or thigh

manifestations.description: unsightly scar on the right ankle and foot
mild hypersensitivity at the skin graft donor site in the right thigh
pain in the bone under the grafted site on rough contact
8% impairment of the whole person resulting from the traffic accident

treatments_received: debridement and split-thickness skin graft (31 October 2004)
cast support for right foot and ankle (on discharge)
treatments_future: possible further skin flap / replacement with skin flap (cosmetic/plastic surgery)

losses.description: The unsightly scar in the right ankle and foot and the donor region would be socially awkward when she puts on shoes without socks, during swimming and in communal changing rooms.
Donor site scarring on the right thigh (8 cm x 7 cm).
She will also not be expected to pursue a career as a photographic or fashion model or jobs that require a normal looking ankle and foot.
